pages.title: Treatments
pages.content:
01 / 04

Fertility tests

Most journeys start with a clear picture. A fertility assessment looks at both partners: an AMH blood test, an ultrasound scan of the ovaries, a hormone panel on cycle day 2–5 and a semen analysis.

Results come back within 5 working days and are explained in a 30-minute plan review, which is included in the fee.

  • You have been trying for a year or more
  • You are over 35 and want to know where you stand
  • You are thinking about the future and want facts first

Read about the tests →

02 / 04

IUI

Intrauterine insemination places prepared sperm in the womb around ovulation. It is a gentler first step when the tubes are open and the sperm count is adequate.

We monitor the cycle with scans, time the insemination to the day and keep medication to the minimum that works.

  • Mild male-factor findings
  • Unexplained difficulty conceiving
  • Using donor sperm

See the IUI fee →

03 / 04

IVF and ICSI

In vitro fertilisation brings egg and sperm together in the laboratory. ICSI places a single sperm into each mature egg, and is added when the semen analysis suggests it.

A cycle takes about five weeks from first injection to pregnancy test. We explain every stage before it starts.

  • Blocked or damaged tubes
  • Several unsuccessful IUI cycles
  • Lower egg reserve or male-factor findings

IVF step by step →

04 / 04

Egg and embryo freezing

Freezing keeps eggs or embryos for later. Some people freeze before treatment that may affect fertility, some because the timing of life asks for it.

One cycle takes about two weeks. Storage is €350 per year and we confirm it in writing every year.

  • Planning to have children later
  • Before medical treatment
  • Embryos left after an IVF cycle

Egg freezing fees →

pages.title: IVF step by step
pages.content:
An IVF cycle has six stages. Here is each one in plain words, with the time it usually takes. Your doctor may change the order or dose for you; the timings are typical, not promises.

Stage 01

Stimulation

10–12 days. Daily injections encourage several eggs to mature at once. A nurse shows you the pen on the first day, and most people find it easier than expected.

Stage 02

Monitoring

3–4 scans. Short ultrasound scans and a blood test check how the follicles are growing. The dose is adjusted after each one, so no two cycles look exactly alike.

Stage 03

Egg collection

about 20 minutes. Under light sedation, a fine needle collects the eggs through the vaginal wall. You rest for an hour and go home the same day.

Stage 04

In the laboratory

5 days. The eggs are fertilised and the embryos are kept in incubators. Our lead embryologist phones you each morning with an update.

Stage 05

Transfer

about 15 minutes. One embryo is placed in the womb with a thin catheter, guided by ultrasound. No sedation is needed and you can walk out afterwards.

Stage 06

Pregnancy test

12 days later. A blood test confirms the result. Whatever it shows, a nurse calls you and we book a conversation about what comes next.

What a cycle feels like

Tired, hopeful, busy

Most people say the injections are the smallest part. The waiting is the hardest. We keep an on-call nurse for patients in a cycle, and you can phone with any question, at any hour.

Plan for a light week around egg collection and a calm day after the transfer. Most people go back to work the next day.

See what it costs →

A typical cycle

Five weeks, one page

Week 1–2: injections, scans on days 5 and 8. Week 2–3: trigger injection, egg collection. Week 3: embryo culture, phone updates. Week 4: transfer. Week 5: pregnancy test 12 days after transfer.

pages.title: Fertility tests
pages.content:
A fertility assessment answers four questions: are eggs being released, is there enough sperm, are the tubes open, and is the womb healthy. It costs €420 for a couple and results arrive within 5 working days.

AMH blood test

A hormone made by the small follicles in the ovaries. It gives a general idea of egg reserve, not whether you can conceive.

Antral follicle scan

A short vaginal ultrasound that counts the resting follicles and looks at the womb and ovaries.

Hormone panel, day 2–5

A blood sample early in your cycle that shows FSH, LH and oestradiol, and how well the signals between brain and ovaries work.

Semen analysis

Counts, movement and shape of sperm after two to five days of abstinence. If the result is unusual we repeat it before drawing a conclusion.

Tubal check (HyCoSy)

A scan with a little fluid that shows whether the fallopian tubes are open. It takes about 15 minutes and feels like a strong period cramp.

When results arrive

Five working days

You will not wait for a letter. A doctor phones or meets you for a 30-minute plan review, which is included in the fee. If everything looks typical we say so; if not, we explain the options without rushing you.

The tests do not need to be done together. Many couples start with the semen analysis, which is quick and gives useful information on day one.

Book a first consultation →

pages.title: Fees & funding
pages.content:
Price list

Every price, in euros

The same figures on the website and at the desk. No outcomes are guaranteed; every plan is individual.

First consultation, both partners, 60 min

Fertility assessment (AMH, scan, hormone panel, semen analysis)

Storage per year

€350

Medication is billed by the pharmacy and is usually €1,200–2,500 per IVF cycle. We give you an estimate before you start.

What is included

First consultation, both partners, 60 min

Both partners, 60 minutes with a doctor. We go through your history, explain what the tests can and cannot show and agree on a next step. Not every first consultation leads to treatment.

Fertility assessment (AMH, scan, hormone panel, semen analysis)

AMH blood test, antral follicle scan, day 2–5 hormone panel and semen analysis for one couple. Results in 5 working days; the plan review is included.

IUI cycle

Cycle monitoring scans, the insemination itself and the sperm preparation. Medication is separate.

IVF cycle (monitoring, egg collection, lab, one fresh transfer)

Monitoring scans, egg collection under light sedation, laboratory work, five days of embryo culture and one fresh transfer. Medication is separate.

ICSI add-on

Added to an IVF cycle when a single sperm is placed into each mature egg.

Frozen embryo transfer

Preparation scans, thawing and one transfer of a frozen embryo.

Egg freezing cycle

Monitoring, egg collection under light sedation and freezing of the mature eggs. Storage is separate.

Storage per year

Embryos or eggs, per year, billed on the anniversary of freezing.

Paying and cancelling

Treatment fees are paid in two parts: half when you book the cycle and the rest on the day of egg collection or transfer. If you cancel before the first injection we return the booking part in full, less €150 for the preparation already done.

We are not an insurer and cannot promise that yours will contribute. We will give you an itemised receipt for each visit so you can ask. Please check your own cover first.

Ask us about funding →

pages.title: Questions, answered first
pages.content:
Before you start

Tests

IVF and treatment

Costs and practical

Before you start

When should we see a doctor?

If you are under 35 and have tried for a year without success, or over 35 and have tried for six months, a first consultation makes sense. Sooner if you have irregular cycles or a known condition.

Do we both have to come?

Please do, if you can. Fertility is a shared matter and half of findings involve the male partner. If one of you cannot attend, we meet by video.

What happens at the first consultation?

A 60-minute conversation with a doctor about your history, followed by a plan. No tests are done on the day unless you want them. It costs €180.

Can single people or same-sex couples be patients?

Yes. We treat everyone who wants a child, including single parents by choice and same-sex couples, with donor sperm or eggs from licensed banks.

Do I need a referral?

No. You can book directly. If you have earlier results, bring them; they save you repeat tests.

How long does a typical journey take?

Tests and plan review take about three weeks. An IUI cycle takes two weeks and an IVF cycle about five. Some people need several attempts and some never need treatment.

Will our details stay private?

Yes. Your records are kept on a secured system and shared only with the people involved in your care. We never talk to your employer or family.

Tests

Do we both need tests before starting?

In almost every case. The assessment covers an AMH test, a scan, a hormone panel and a semen analysis, for €420 in total.

Do the tests hurt?

The scans are uncomfortable rather than painful. The tubal check feels like a strong period cramp for a few minutes.

What does the AMH level tell us?

It estimates egg reserve. It does not predict whether you will conceive naturally, so we read it with your age and scan findings.

How should I prepare for the semen analysis?

Two to five days without ejaculation, a clean container from us, and delivery within an hour. A private room is available.

When do I have the scans?

The antral follicle scan and hormone panel are done on cycle day 2–5. We fit them around your work where we can.

How quickly do we get results?

Within 5 working days. A doctor explains them in a 30-minute plan review included in the fee.

Are the results shared with anyone?

No. They go to you and your doctor. With your written permission we send them to your family doctor.

IVF and treatment

What is the difference between IUI and IVF?

IUI places prepared sperm in the womb. IVF collects eggs and fertilises them in the laboratory. IUI is gentler; IVF is used when IUI is unlikely to help.

How many injections will I need?

Usually one a day for 10–12 days, plus a trigger injection. A nurse teaches you on the first day and is on call for questions.

Does egg collection hurt?

It takes about 20 minutes under light sedation. Most people feel period-like cramps for a day.

Can I work during a cycle?

Most people do. Plan time for the scans, usually 3–4 short visits, and take the day of egg collection off.

What is ICSI?

A single sperm is injected into each mature egg. It is added to an IVF cycle for €1,100 when the semen analysis suggests it.

How many embryos are transferred?

Usually one. We explain the reasons and the risks of twins before the transfer.

What if the cycle does not work?

We meet to look at what we learned and talk through options. There is no obligation to continue, and no pressure.

How long can eggs and embryos be stored?

As long as you pay the annual €350 storage fee and keep your consent up to date, within the limits of local law.

Costs and practical

How much does an IVF cycle cost?

€4,800, covering monitoring, egg collection, lab work and one fresh transfer. Medication is billed separately by the pharmacy.

How much is medication?

Usually €1,200–2,500 per IVF cycle, depending on your dose. We give you an estimate before you start.

Do we pay everything up front?

No. Treatment is paid in two parts: half at booking and the rest on the day of egg collection or transfer.

What if we cancel?

Before the first injection we return the booking part, less €150 for preparation. After that, fees for work already done are not refundable.

Where are you and when are you open?

14 Harbour Lane, Lindenport, second floor with lift. Mon–Fri 7:30–18:00 and Sat 8:00–12:00 for scans and collections.

Do you have parking?

There is public parking two minutes’ walk away and a tram stop outside. Please allow ten minutes to find the lift.

Still not here? Ask us. We will add it.

pages.title: About our approach
pages.content:
Since 2011

A clinic that answers first

Sora Fertility Centre opened on the second floor of 14 Harbour Lane in 2011 with three treatment rooms and a laboratory. Dr. Helena Marsh had spent years in larger hospital units and wanted a place where a patient never had to wait for a letter to learn what a scan showed.

We have grown to seven people and a second scan room, but kept the rule: answers first, plan second. Our laboratory follows written standards for air quality, temperature and double checking of every dish, and our lead embryologist reviews them each month.

A letter from our director

When I opened Sora in 2011 I wrote down one rule: answer the question first. Over the years people have told us that the hardest part of fertility care is not the injections but the not knowing, so we try to say what we know, what we do not and what we would do in your place.

We are a small clinic. The same seven people see you from the first scan to the pregnancy test. If you phone, one of us answers. If a result is difficult, you hear it from a doctor, in a room, with time.

We never promise an outcome. We promise to explain, to be on call and to tell you the truth gently.

Dr. Helena Marsh, Medical Director

How we work

Three habits shape the clinic. We write down every question you ask and answer it in writing. We explain costs before treatment, not after. And we agree with you when to stop as clearly as when to start.

Meet the team →

pages.title: Patient stories
pages.content:
01 / 03

Mei and Jonas

“The second cycle was calmer than the first, mostly because we knew what each week would look like. Nadia’s phone calls in the middle of the laboratory days kept us from imagining the worst.”

Mei and Jonas came to Sora after a first IVF cycle elsewhere. They told us they wanted the same information, only earlier.

02 / 03

Priya

“I froze my eggs at 36 because I wanted the choice, not because I had a plan. The nurse showed me the pen on the first day and I did the rest at home. It was less dramatic than I feared.”

Priya’s cycle took about two weeks from the first injection to collection.

03 / 03

Claire and Sam

“We started with the tests, and the plan review was the first time anyone had explained our results in words we could use. We moved to IUI after that, with no pressure about what came next.”

Claire and Sam had been trying for eighteen months when they booked a first consultation.

These stories are shared with consent and shortened. Every journey is individual; they are not predictions, and no outcome is guaranteed.

Book a first consultation →

pages.title: First consultation & contact
pages.content:
First visit

The first sixty minutes

A doctor meets you both, usually in the consultation room facing the window, and listens first. We go through history, any earlier tests and what you hope for.

You leave with a written plan and a price for each step. There is no obligation, and no tests are done on the day unless you ask. The fee is €180.

Fees in full →

What to bring

Before you come

  • Photo ID for each partner
  • Any earlier test results or scan reports
  • A list of medicines you take, with doses
  • Your questions, written down, as many as you like

We will ask permission before we write anything down.

Find us

14 Harbour Lane, Lindenport

Second floor, lift access. Tram stop outside; public parking two minutes’ walk away.

Mon–Fri 7:30–18:00
Saturday 8:00–12:00, scans and collections
Sunday closed

Phone line Mon–Fri 8:00–17:00 · +00 1234 5678. An on-call nurse is available to patients in a cycle.

Harbour Lane, Lindenport

Ask us anything

Leave a name and email and a nurse will call you back within one working day.

Read the questions we hear most →

pages.title: Clinic letter
pages.content: Four times a year we send a short letter: one question we were asked, one thing we changed, and any news about opening hours. No marketing, and you can leave with one click.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
This sample page explains, in plain words, how a clinic handles your details. Replace it with your own policy before going live.

What we keep

Your name, contact details, medical history, test results and the notes from your visits. We keep them so we can care for you safely and as the law requires.

Who sees it

Only the people involved in your care. We share results with your family doctor only with your written permission. We never sell data.

Your rights

You can ask to see, correct or take a copy of your records. Write to the front desk at 14 Harbour Lane, Lindenport.

posts.title: What to ask at your first consultation
posts.excerpt: A short list of questions, and why writing yours down helps.
posts.content:
Most people arrive at their first appointment with a list. Some of it is medical, some of it is practical and some of it is the question underneath: are we too late? We try to answer all three.

Before you come, write down every question, even the ones you think are silly. We keep them in your notes and answer each in writing. You do not need to know medical words.

Bring any earlier results, a list of medicines and, if you can, your partner. The consultation takes sixty minutes, costs €180 and ends with a written plan.

Afterwards you decide. Some people book tests the same week, and some go home to think. Both are fine.
